subject: Pilot Order — DPA reconciliation, SCCs and EU transfer carveouts
messages:

Subject: Pilot Order SFO-129 — initial DPA checklist and SCCs question

Hi Sara / Evolve team,

Thanks again for confirming the pilot order (SFO-129). Attaching our latest Order Form (OrderForm_SFO-129_v2.pdf) and a blank DPA for your review. Before we move to signature, can you confirm:

- Whether you have standard changes to the SCCs you require when we act as processor.
- Any EU-local transfer carveouts or additional restrictions (exports to non-EEA subsidiaries).
- If you need a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) completed as part of contracting.

If easier, we can take these one item at a time — happy to jump on a 30-min call.

Attachments: OrderForm_SFO-129_v2.pdf

Thanks,
Lauren

From: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@evolvehealth.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@evolvehealth.com>
Date: 2025-07-15T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot Order SFO-129 — initial DPA checklist and SCCs question

Hi Lauren,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. We ran this quickly through our legal team and attached our redlines to your DPA (DPA_v3_redline.docx). High-level items:

1) Roles: we marked several clauses where we think Evolve will need to be "controller" for certain categories (patient identifiers used for analytics) — please confirm Redwood's proposed role mapping.
2) SCCs: we prefer the updated EU SCCs executed as Addendum A. We flagged two places where your template departs (reciprocal audit language and onward transfer wording).
3) Transfer carveouts: one of our affiliates in APAC requires limited access to de-identified records; this is currently treated as an export in our policy. We need clarity on your KMS key control and whether encryption-at-rest keys are customer-managed.

We can do a call Tues/Wed next week. Also looping in Tom Grant (outside counsel) for now — he may propose narrow language on the audit and liability sections.

Attachments: DPA_v3_redline.docx

Thanks,
Sara Dunne
Head of Legal Operations, EvolveHealth
S.Dunne@evolvehealth.com
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2025-07-16T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA redlines from EvolveHealth / need review

Karthik / Monica — forwarding Sara's redlines and notes from Evolve. Can you:

- Review the attached DPA_v3_redline.docx and call out any terms that are likely to be non-starters (esp. SCC deviations, audit reciprocity, liability caps tied to export controls).
- Draft suggested language for role mapping (processor subprocessor matrix) we can send back.
- Advise whether we need to produce a TIA; if so, what template and timeline.

I copied Sara so you can follow up directly if needed.

Attachments: DPA_v3_redline.docx

— Lauren
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@evolvehealth.com>
Date: 2025-07-17T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines from EvolveHealth / need review

Thanks Lauren — quick notes after reviewing DPA_v3_redline.docx:

- Roles: we should propose a two-column role map (Redwood = processor for inference and embeddings; Evolve = controller for customer PII ingestion and identity resolution). I'll attach a one-page mapping for ease of sign-off.
- SCCs deviations flagged: the audit reciprocity ask (Section 8) is broader than industry norm. Recommend we offer a scoped audit response (desk review + evidence package) instead of full reciprocal audits.
- Onward transfers: their APAC carveout appears to request persistent re-export rights to a third-party affiliate. We should ask for a minimal TIA documenting transfer legal basis and safeguards rather than broad carveouts.
- KMS: we can support customer-managed CMEK for on-prem/private deployments; for hosted pilot, we provide robust key separation but not customer KMS for the initial pilot. Propose language to be explicit about pilot scope.

Next steps: 1) I'll draft redline suggestions and a short TIA template; 2) we should loop in Tom Grant only if Evolve insists on full audit reciprocity.

Attachments: (internal) role_mapping_onepager.docx

— Karthik
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@evolvehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@evolvehealth.com>
Date: 2025-07-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot Order SFO-129 — proposed consolidated response and next steps

Hi Sara — thanks for the redlines and context. Attached are: 1) SCCs-Implementation-Notes.xlsx which maps each SCC clause to proposed Redwood language; 2) our consolidated redline for the DPA (embedded in DPA_v3_redline.docx) reflecting Karthik's recommendations.

Key points we propose:
- Role map: we propose Redwood = processor (inference, hosting), Evolve = controller (ingestion, identity). Please confirm acceptance.
- Audits: offer scoped compliance package (SOC2 report, dataflow diagram, subprocessor roster, desk review evidence) in lieu of reciprocal on-site audit during the pilot.
- Transfers: for the pilot, we will accept a targeted TIA covering the APAC affiliate access scenario. Karthik will share a short TIA template this week. For long-term deployments, we'll evaluate CMEK options.

If this is acceptable, I can circulate an updated Order Form with the DPA redlines and a DocuSign link to speed signature. Proposed next step: 30-min call Thursday (07/24) to iron out the TIA specifics.

Attachments: SCCs-Implementation-Notes.xlsx, DPA_v3_redline.docx

Best,
Lauren
From: Sara Dunne <sara.dunne@evolvehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@evolvehealth.com>, Tom Grant <tgrant@lawfirmblake.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-22T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot Order SFO-129 — proposed consolidated response and next steps

Lauren — this is helpful, appreciate the clarity. We reviewed internally:

- Role map: accepted as proposed for the pilot.
- Audits: procurement is comfortable with the scoped compliance package for the pilot; they asked for a checklist of required evidence (SOC2, subprocessor list, data flow diagram).
- TIA: we'll accept the short TIA for the pilot. Tom may follow up with a couple of drafting suggestions but nothing blocking.

Procurement will send a DocuSign request once we receive the updated Order Form with the attached DPA redlines. Also, can you confirm the expected delivery of the evidence package and whether any items will take >2 weeks to produce?
